name: Nail-Patella-Like Renal Disease

criteria.description: Presence of nail dysplasia including absent, hypoplastic, or dystrophic nails
Hypoplasia or aplasia of the patella confirmed by clinical or radiological examination
Evidence of renal disease such as proteinuria, hematuria, or progressive renal insufficiency
Radiographic presence of iliac horns on pelvic X-ray
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of nail dysplasia, patellar hypoplasia/aplasia, and renal involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for LMX1B mutations can confirm diagnosis

laboratory: Persistent proteinuria and hematuria on urinalysis
Elevated serum creatinine in progressive renal disease
imaging: Pelvic X-ray showing bilateral iliac horns
Knee radiographs demonstrating patellar hypoplasia or aplasia
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic basement membrane changes on renal biopsy
Absence of nail and patellar abnormalities
Primary renal pathology without musculoskeletal or nail abnormalities
No family history of nail-patella syndrome features

redFlags: Onset of glaucoma or visual impairment
references: Bongers EMHFJ, et al. Nail-patella syndrome: clinical and molecular findings. J Med Genet. 2002.
Lemley KV, et al. Renal involvement in nail-patella syndrome. Pediatr Nephrol. 2000.
